title: Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) - Customer Feedback Roundtable
summary: Roundtable with 3 friendly customers plus Redwood DevEx/Obs/Support to review the internal beta Quickstart Templates (Python + TypeScript RAG/agent). Main feedback: onboarding is close, but users get stuck on (1) OTel collector/exporter config, (2) streaming disconnects behind proxies, (3) default concurrency causing 429s, and (4) confusion around “agents” terminology and tool schema failures. Customers want clearer “prod path” deployment guidance (Docker/K8s/VPC), and a simple way to verify observability end-to-end (a script and a checklist). Session ended with a prioritized fix list and owners.
topics: Observability expectations (metrics, traces, logs) and cardinality concerns
Streaming robustness behind proxies and reconnect behavior
Safe defaults: timeouts, retries, max_tokens, concurrency limits
Deployment recipes: Docker, Kubernetes, VPC/private considerations
Tool calling / schema validation failure modes and UX
next_steps: Redwood to ship a “verify observability” script + README section (how to confirm traces/metrics/logs locally).
DevEx to change default concurrency/backoff to reduce 429s in self-serve accounts, and document recommended QPS.
Observability team to provide a minimal local OTel collector config + troubleshooting flow (common exporter/auth mistakes).
DevEx to update template telemetry tagging to be opt-in by default and avoid custom headers where possible.
Docs to clarify terminology (“agent loop” vs “workflow”) and add a tool schema failure troubleshooting page.
Redwood to publish a deployment options matrix with clear hosted vs dedicated vs private notes (k8s and VPC).
action_items: Monica Patel - Update template defaults: lower concurrency, adjust retry/backoff guidance, add max in-flight guard (due 2025-03-06)
Wei Chen - Rewrite README Quickstart steps with an explicit “Success checklist” and add “agent loop” terminology note (due 2025-03-07)
Allison Grant - Provide canonical OTel attributes + a “low-cardinality safe set” section for templates (due 2025-03-08)
Sergio Costa - Add an example dashboard screenshot set + link to dashboard pack in docs (due 2025-03-11)
Dev Patel - Draft a support playbook for top 5 template issues (401/429/stream disconnect/collector auth/tool schema) (due 2025-03-12)
Renee Sullivan - Follow up with customers for 30-min validation after fixes land; schedule sessions (due 2025-03-14)
questions: Open questions captured: Should telemetry tagging rely on headers or query/body tags to avoid proxy blocks? What’s the minimum “prod” deployment recipe we can stand behind (Docker + k8s)? Do we want one hosted vector DB adapter in v1, or keep only local to reduce dependency surface? Can we add a “doctor” check for OTel collector reachability that doesn’t require privileges?
transcript:
Meeting Header
Recorded: 2025-02-27 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Title: Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) - Customer Feedback Roundtable
Attendees (Redwood): Renee Sullivan, Monica Patel, Wei Chen, Allison Grant, Sergio Costa, Dev Patel
Attendees (Customers): Jamie Park (Arcadia Search), Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search), Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial), Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry), Priya Nair (DevFoundry)

Action items (auto-generated)
- Monica: adjust defaults around concurrency/retry and document recommended QPS
- Allison/Sergio: tighten OTel guidance and ship “known good” collector configs
- Wei: docs/README cleanup, “agents” terminology, troubleshooting
- Dev: support playbook

---

[00:00] Renee Sullivan: Cool, alright. Thanks everyone for making time. This is a friendly-customer roundtable on the Quickstart Templates beta, specifically RAG plus the agent loop template in Python and TypeScript. Goal is pretty simple: what tripped you up, what you’d expect for prod, and what’s missing in observability and deployment.

[00:21] Renee Sullivan: Quick intros, and then we’ll do like, 10 minutes per area and end with a prioritized list. Monica and Wei are here from DevEx, Allison and Sergio from observability, Dev from support.

[00:35] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): I’m Jamie, I run the doc search product engineering side. We tried the Python template.

[00:41] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Vikram, staff engineer. I looked at the TypeScript one too.

[00:45] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Lena, platform engineering. Our interest is VPC / private deploy eventually, but we prototype on hosted.

[00:53] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Tomás, CTO. We’re small, we want fast. We tried to get to first demo with the template.

[00:59] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Priya, ML engineer. I cared mostly about eval hooks and tool calling failures.

[01:05] Monica Patel: Awesome, thanks. Monica from DevEx, engineering lead on templates.

[01:08] Wei Chen: Wei, tech writing. I own the walkthrough docs and troubleshooting pages.

[01:12] Allison Grant: Allison, observability standards.

[01:14] Sergio Costa: Sergio, dashboards/alerts.

[01:16] Dev Patel: Dev, support ops.

[01:20] Renee Sullivan: Great. Let’s start with onboarding: time-to-first-success. Like, from clone/init to first meaningful response. What was it?

[01:31] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Honestly, close. Like 20–30 minutes to run it locally, but we stalled on the telemetry / OpenTelemetry part. The app ran, but we didn’t see traces in the place we expected.

[01:47] Renee Sullivan: Was that local collector or exporting to your backend?

[01:50] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Local collector with docker compose. The README says “start the collector” and then “run the app”, but it wasn’t obvious how to validate it. Like, did it work? Is it emitting metrics? It’s kind of… you know, it’s invisible.

[02:07] Sergio Costa: That’s helpful. We have a “dashboard pack” but it’s not super discoverable in beta.

[02:13] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): We also got 429s pretty quickly. I think the template default concurrency is a bit high for a new hosted account. We had like, I don’t know, 5 parallel requests from the UI test and it started backing off but not enough.

[02:29] Monica Patel: Yep, we’ve seen that. We set it for “snappy demo” but it’s too aggressive on self-serve tiers.

[02:36] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): For us it was even simpler. The “init” flow was good, but the env vars… we missed one, and it errored, but the error didn’t tell me exactly what to do. It said something like “missing config” and then like a stack trace. Not the end of the world, but it’s not beginner-friendly.

[02:56] Dev Patel: That’s consistent with tickets we saw internally. People want “here’s the exact env var, here’s an example value”.

[03:04] Wei Chen: Noted.

[03:06] Renee Sullivan: Priya, you mentioned eval hooks and tool calling.

[03:10] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Yeah. The eval hook exists, which is great. But it wasn’t obvious what “good” looks like. Like do I run it and get a JSON? A score? And the tool calling—when the tool schema validation fails, we got a pretty cryptic error. I think it said “parse error” and then dumped some JSON-ish text.

[03:33] Monica Patel: Was it the structured output parse for tools?

[03:35] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): I think so. The model returned slightly different keys than the schema expected, and then it just… stopped. It would be better to show a “model returned invalid tool args” message and maybe log the raw but redacted payload.

[03:51] Allison Grant: +1, but we have to be careful about logging too much. Redaction rules.

[03:56] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): For us, any raw tool args can include PII. So, redaction is not optional. But we still need enough to debug.

[04:07] Renee Sullivan: That’s a good segue. Let’s move to observability expectations. What do you want out of the box?

[04:14] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Minimum: request ID correlation between app logs and the inference request. If we open a support ticket, we need an ID we can hand you. Then: latency breakdown. Not just total. We want retrieval time vs model time vs tool time.

[04:32] Sergio Costa: That’s exactly how our dashboards are structured: “RAG breakdown”, “tool failure rate”, token economics.

[04:38] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Great, but I didn’t see the mapping in docs. Like, “these spans feed this dashboard.” Also, cardinality. Please don’t tag every user ID in traces by default.

[04:51] Allison Grant: Yep. We’ve been pushing a “low-cardinality safe set.” Things like template_name, template_version, model, route, status_code, but not arbitrary query strings or user identifiers.

[05:05] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Question: are you expecting us to run our own collector in prod? Or is Redwood doing it?

[05:11] Allison Grant: For template apps, we assume you’ll emit OTel to your own collector and then to wherever (Datadog, Grafana, etc). For Redwood Console specifically, you’ll see the inference-side metrics in our system, but your app spans are yours.

[05:26] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Got it. Then the docs should say “this is app-level telemetry, not Redwood Console by default.” We had some confusion.

[05:35] Wei Chen: That’s fair. We can make it explicit.

[05:38] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Also, the “verify it works” thing. Like a script that checks “collector reachable”, “sent one trace”, “sent one metric”. Even if it’s basic.

[05:50] Sergio Costa: We actually have a small verification script in our examples repo, but it’s not wired into templates.

[05:56] Monica Patel: We can ship it with the templates as `scripts/verify_observability`.

[06:02] Renee Sullivan: Great. Let’s talk streaming. We saw some chatter about disconnects behind proxies.

[06:10] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Yeah, that was us. We put it behind a corporate-ish proxy (not even super locked down) and streaming would just cut out. The UI would hang.

[06:22] Speaker 1: Was it SSE?

[06:24] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Yeah, server-sent events. It would start, then like 10 seconds later, done. No error.

[06:33] Monica Patel: We do have a reconnect strategy in the template, but it might be too optimistic or missing the edge case where the proxy strips headers.

[06:41] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Related: we had an issue with a telemetry header. I don’t remember the exact name, but our API gateway rejected unknown headers. It was returning a 4xx before it even hit your endpoint.

[06:56] Renee Sullivan: That’s important. We’ve been debating header-based tagging for adoption metrics.

[07:02] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): If it’s optional and clearly documented, fine. But default-on extra headers will break in enterprise networks. Like, guaranteed.

[07:13] Allison Grant: And also privacy. If it’s a tag, it must not include anything sensitive.

[07:18] Monica Patel: Understood. We can make telemetry tagging opt-in, and prefer a standard header if possible, or even put it in the user-agent string rather than custom headers.

[07:30] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Yeah user-agent is usually allowed. Custom headers are the ones that get blocked.

[07:36] Dev Patel: From support perspective, “mysterious 4xx due to proxy header policy” is a nightmare. So opt-in is key.

[07:45] Renee Sullivan: Let’s go into safe defaults: timeouts, retries, max tokens, concurrency, cost caps. What do you expect?

[07:56] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Max tokens default should be conservative. We had a run where it basically rambled. If you’re trying to be production-minded, cap it and show where to change it.

[08:08] Monica Patel: We cap, but maybe it’s too high right now.

[08:12] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Also, “retry on streaming” is tricky. If it retries, does it duplicate tool calls? Does it double charge? Like I need it to be safe.

[08:26] Monica Patel: Right now, the template’s approach is: retry only before the first token is received. After you’ve started streaming, it fails fast and surfaces a specific error. But we need to document that clearly.

[08:40] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): That’s good. But we didn’t know. We saw backoff logs and couldn’t tell what it was doing.

[08:47] Allison Grant: Logging should indicate: “retrying pre-stream”, “stream interrupted”, and include request id.

[08:54] Dev Patel: And a human-friendly remediation: “If behind proxy, disable buffering, ensure SSE is allowed.” Stuff like that.

[09:05] Wei Chen: We can add a troubleshooting section: “Streaming disconnects / proxies.”

[09:11] Renee Sullivan: Nice. Deployment needs: what do you want to see in templates? Docker, Fly, k8s, VPC, on-prem… we can’t do everything.

[09:22] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): For us, it’s Kubernetes. If it’s a “prod-minded” template, we need at least a reference manifest. Doesn’t need to be perfect, but like: deployment, service, env vars, secret mounting, and how to run the OTel collector. And some notes for private/VPC where DNS and egress are restricted.

[09:44] Sergio Costa: The collector in k8s is a whole can of worms, but we have a minimal config.

[09:49] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Minimal is fine. But please specify what’s required. Like “OTLP endpoint” and “auth” is where people mess up.

[09:59] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): We’re more mid-market. Docker compose was fine for local. For production we might use ECS, but k8s docs still help.

[10:08] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): We just want one push-button deploy path. Fly.io or Render is great for that. But the template should say “this is dev/prototype, not enterprise.”

[10:21] Renee Sullivan: That’s aligned with our plan: provide a few recipes and label them.

[10:27] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): One more: vector store adapter scope. We didn’t want to run Pinecone just to try a template. Local default is good. But show me where I swap it. The interface looked okay.

[10:41] Monica Patel: We’re keeping local default, plus a placeholder adapter that’s optional.

[10:46] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Local is fine for demos, but for evals we need determinism. If retrieval results change run to run, tests are flaky.

[10:56] Monica Patel: Good point. We can seed chunking and make ordering deterministic. And for eval mode, fixed corpus.

[11:05] Renee Sullivan: Let’s dig into “agents” terminology. We’ve heard some confusion.

[11:11] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): “Agent” is overloaded. We expected like, multi-step planning, memory, and like tool orchestration. The template is more like a controlled loop with tool calls. Which is fine! But call it “agent loop” or “workflow.”

[11:27] Wei Chen: We have an internal thread about this. We can rename in docs to “tool-using workflow (agent loop)” and keep “agents” as a keyword.

[11:36] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Yeah because my CEO brain reads “agents” and expects magic. Then it’s like “oh it’s a loop.”

[11:45] (crosstalk)

[11:46] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): The important part is the guardrails. Like max iterations. That was good.

[11:52] Monica Patel: We cap at 5 iterations by default.

[11:55] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Perfect. Also tool output size limit. We hit a case where a tool returned huge text and then the model choked.

[12:05] Monica Patel: We have a limit, but maybe it’s too high.

[12:09] Allison Grant: Also log a metric for “tool_output_truncated” so people know it happened.

[12:16] Sergio Costa: That would feed into the tool failure dashboard.

[12:21] Renee Sullivan: Switching to observability detail: which metrics do you care about most? If we had to pick 5.

[12:28] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): 1) request latency p50/p95, 2) error rate by class (auth/quota/network/tool/retrieval), 3) token usage per request, 4) retrieval hit rate or “empty retrieval” rate, 5) tool failure rate.

[12:49] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Add “cache hit” if you have it. But I know that might be more on your side.

[12:55] Allison Grant: Some is inference-side, but app can log whether it used a local cache or prefix cache hints. We’re cautious.

[13:04] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Tracing: the span names should be intuitive. Like `rag.retrieve`, `llm.generate`, `tool.call`. Don’t call it `pipeline.step2`.

[13:16] Allison Grant: Agreed. We have conventions.

[13:19] Wei Chen: We should document that mapping. “When you run the template, you’ll see spans: …”

[13:25] Renee Sullivan: I want to make sure we capture what blocked you most. Let’s go around: top 1–2 pain points.

[13:33] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): 1) Observability setup validation. 2) Confusion about whether traces should show in Redwood Console.

[13:41] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): 1) 429 rate limits from defaults. 2) Header/proxy weirdness.

[13:48] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): 1) Need k8s/VPC deploy notes. 2) Need explicit redaction guidance; don’t log prompts by default.

[13:58] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): 1) Streaming disconnect behavior unclear. 2) Env var errors not friendly.

[14:06] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): 1) Tool schema validation errors are confusing. 2) Evals need clearer output and deterministic mode.

[14:16] Monica Patel: This is super actionable.

[14:19] Renee Sullivan: We have time. Let’s deep dive 429/defaults, then OTel collector issues, then tool schema UX.

[14:27] Monica Patel: On 429: what concurrency were you running?

[14:31] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): We had a simple script firing 10 queries with `Promise.all`. Probably 10 parallel. The UI also did prefetch.

[14:40] Monica Patel: That’ll do it. Our template had default `MAX_IN_FLIGHT=8` for the demo feel. We can lower to 2 or 3 and use jittered backoff.

[14:52] Dev Patel: Also add a log line like “You may be on a self-serve tier; reduce concurrency.” People don’t know what 429 means.

[15:00] Wei Chen: And a troubleshooting entry: “429 Quota / Rate limiting.”

[15:06] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Another thing: when it backs off, it should not spam logs every 100ms. We saw a lot of noise.

[15:14] Monica Patel: We can rate-limit the log or log only on retry attempt count.

[15:18] Allison Grant: For metrics, a counter `http.client.retries` with label `reason=429` is fine, but keep labels controlled.

[15:28] Renee Sullivan: OTel collector issues: what happened exactly?

[15:32] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): We ran docker compose, but the exporter was pointing to `localhost:4317` from inside the container, I think. So it couldn’t reach. The README didn’t explain networking.

[15:45] Sergio Costa: Ah yep. Common. We need to have “if app runs on host, use localhost; if in docker, use collector service name.”

[15:55] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): We also had auth confusion. One doc said “set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS” and another said “set token env var.” We guessed.

[16:05] Allison Grant: We should provide a minimal “known good” matrix: local dev with no auth, and production with headers. And include examples.

[16:14] Wei Chen: I can add a table in the docs.

[16:17] Dev Patel: Plus: a “doctor” command could check collector connectivity. If you have a CLI. Do you?

[16:24] Monica Patel: We do have a CLI in progress. It can validate env vars and ping endpoints. We can add a collector check.

[16:32] Renee Sullivan: That’d be huge for support deflection.

[16:36] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): On tool schema: what I want is error taxonomy. Like “TOOL_SCHEMA_INVALID” and “TOOL_OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE” not a generic “parse error.”

[16:49] Monica Patel: We have an error taxonomy draft. We can align.

[16:53] Allison Grant: And in logs, we should include `error.type` and `error.code` and `request.id`.

[16:59] Sergio Costa: That will make dashboards meaningful too.

[17:03] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Also, if the tool returns invalid JSON, the model might be at fault. But the developer needs to know what to fix. Sometimes it’s the schema, sometimes the prompt.

[17:14] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Exactly. A troubleshooting doc: “if tool args don’t match, tighten schema, add examples.”

[17:22] Wei Chen: I’ll do that.

[17:24] Renee Sullivan: Let’s talk privacy/redaction. Lena, you’re strict here.

[17:30] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Yes. Default logging should never print the entire prompt, retrieval chunks, or tool outputs. I’m okay with hashed IDs or sizes. Like “retrieved 5 chunks, total 12KB.” That’s it.

[17:46] Allison Grant: Our standard is: redact by default, allow opt-in “debug mode” with explicit warning.

[17:52] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): That’s reasonable. We sometimes need to debug, but it should be deliberate.

[17:58] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): For startups we’ll flip debug on, but if it’s not easy, we’ll just add our own logs anyway.

[18:05] Monica Patel: We can add a `LOG_SENSITIVE=false` default and require explicit true.

[18:10] Dev Patel: And put big warnings in README.

[18:14] Renee Sullivan: Deployment: k8s minimal manifests. Are we aligned that we ship it as “reference” not “supported”?

[18:22] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Yes. Just show best practices: secrets, health checks, resource requests, and where to plug OTel.

[18:32] Sergio Costa: We can add a helm-ish snippet, or at least YAML. But minimal.

[18:38] Wei Chen: We also have a deployment options matrix doc idea. I can publish it.

[18:44] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Please add note about VPC/private: “if no outbound internet, you need private endpoints.” Even if it’s a paragraph.

[18:54] Monica Patel: We’ll add a section: hosted vs dedicated vs private, and what changes. Like base URL, auth, collector endpoints.

[19:03] Renee Sullivan: Great. I want to sanity check: is the template itself valuable? Like, would you recommend it to a teammate?

[19:10] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Yes. It’s close to what we’d write. The structure is good.

[19:14] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Same. Especially the retriever interface.

[19:18] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Yeah, if the errors were friendlier. It feels like it’s for engineers, which is fine, but “quickstart” implies smooth.

[19:27] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): The eval hook existing is a differentiator. Most templates don’t bother.

[19:33] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): It’s valuable if the default posture is secure and audit-friendly.

[19:40] Renee Sullivan: Love it. We’re going to use the last ~10 minutes to prioritize fixes. I’m going to read back what I heard, and you can correct.

[19:51] Renee Sullivan: Priority bucket 0 (must-fix before public):
1) Observability “verify” step/script, plus known-good collector configs and networking notes.
2) Change default concurrency/backoff to avoid 429s, and add clear guidance.
3) Make template telemetry tagging opt-in; avoid custom headers that break proxies.
4) Improve tool schema validation errors and troubleshooting; add error codes.
5) Clarify streaming retry behavior and add proxy troubleshooting.

[20:22] Renee Sullivan: Priority bucket 1 (soon after):
6) Add k8s reference manifests + deployment matrix.
7) Improve eval output and deterministic mode.
8) Rename/clarify “agents” terminology in docs.

[20:38] Renee Sullivan: Does that match?

[20:41] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Yes. Put the “verify observability” at the top.

[20:45] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): +1, and the header thing is sneaky but big.

[20:49] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Agree. Also redaction and “no prompts in logs” should be bucket 0.

[20:56] Allison Grant: We can treat that as part of observability config and logging defaults. It’s already mostly there, but we can reinforce.

[21:04] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Streaming/proxy should be bucket 0. That was a blocker.

[21:09] Monica Patel: Noted.

[21:11] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Tool schema errors bucket 0, yes.

[21:16] Wei Chen: I’ll commit to getting the troubleshooting pages updated alongside code changes, otherwise it won’t land.

[21:24] Dev Patel: And I’ll draft a support playbook based on these exact issues.

[21:30] Sergio Costa: From dashboards side, I’ll add screenshots and “what to expect” so people can see success.

[21:38] Renee Sullivan: Perfect. Final question: if we fix these, would you be willing to do a quick re-test in two weeks?

[21:47] Jamie Park (Arcadia Search): Yes.

[21:48] Vikram Desai (Arcadia Search): Yep.

[21:50] Lena Hoffmann (Northbridge Financial): Yes, but I’ll want to see the redaction defaults in writing.

[21:55] Tomás Ribeiro (DevFoundry): Sure.

[21:56] Priya Nair (DevFoundry): Yes.

[21:58] Renee Sullivan: Awesome. We’ll follow up with a short checklist and links. Thanks everyone.

[22:03] (call ends, some side chatter)

Note: Fireflies transcript may omit some mid-call discussion due to crosstalk/overlaps; timestamps are approximate.
